cards.subtitle: Deterministic Sir George Biddell Airy (1835) & Joseph von Fraunhofer (1823) circular-aperture wave diffraction law (first Bessel zero x_1 = 3.831706, angular Airy disk radius theta_1 = 1.21967 * lambda / D = theta_0 * (1 + u) scaling inversely with entrance pupil diameter D(u) = D_0 / (1 + u) and linearly with f-number N(u) = N_0 * (1 + u), locking theta_exact / theta_model = 1.0000x across all 17 stations u in [0.000, 1.000] with 0/17 violated) versus naive geometric-optics fixed PSF (theta = theta_0, which underestimates diffraction Airy radius by 1 + u to 1.2500x at S4, 1.5000x at S8, and 2.0000x / 4x area at S16 across 16/17 stations) and 64-strip Fraunhofer pupil chord quadrature.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Physical camera glare/starburst post-processing, space telescope starlight shaders, optical microscopy, and quadrature CoC + Airy depth-of-field pipelines
Expanding diffraction Airy disk radius linearly with f-number r_Airy = 1.2197 * lambda * N so stopping down to f/16 or f/22 naturally blooms point highlights and softens micro-contrast
Combining geometric defocus circle of confusion and wave diffraction in quadrature r_total = sqrt(r_geom^2 + r_Airy^2)
not_for: Wide-open fast lenses (f/1.4) on out-of-focus backgrounds where geometric bokeh circle of confusion is 50x larger than the Airy disk
